papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that proves Hamiltonian learning is possible from short-time dynamics under two minimal access models (uniform rotations before and after the evolution, or computational-basis preparation and measurement), with sample and evolution-time costs of order one over accuracy squared, and a matching lower bound on total evolution time without interleaved control, with no experiments run.

existing.note: The result holds for generic couplings under Gaussian smoothing (smoothed analysis) and, for the spatially varying case, for open or periodic chains of length at least 4 and rectangles with sides at least 3 (periodic: periods at least 9), with the gauges being Pauli-Z conjugation and time reversal. The two Pauli kinds are X and Z (the rendered abstract reads 'Pauli X/Z interactions'). The authors treat only the nearest-neighbor truncation of the power-law interaction tails of Rydberg and ion platforms and list longer-range interactions as an open problem. Arbitrary Z-basis preparation needs site-resolved bit flips.

papers.what_it_is: A theory and simulation paper that turns the Pauli check sandwiching (PCS) error detection scheme into a distributed protocol for quantum networks and compares its analytic fidelity and postselection rate with BBPSSW entanglement purification.

existing.note: The comparison in Section III.B is analytic: all qubits take the same single-qubit depolarizing noise, with noiseless checks. Section III.B.2 says 'for most of the domain' and compares PCS X&Z (6 qubits) with 2 round (8 qubits) and 3 round (16 qubits) BBPSSW, so the qubit counts are not equal. Fig. 4a compares PCS X with 1 round BBPSSW (4 qubits each).
existing.value: The authors report, from their analytic comparison in which all qubits experience the same depolarization, that PCS outperforms BBPSSW round 1, 2 and 3 in fidelity for a comparable number of input qubits over most of the values of the initial fidelity.
existing.anchor: Section IV Conclusions, p.9; Section III.B.2, p.5; Figure 4 caption, p.6
quotes: In terms of fidelity, it outperforms BBPSSW round 1, 2, and 3 for a comparable number of input qubits and over most of the values of the initial fidelity.
In the PCS analysis, all the qubits experience the same depolarization.
existing.certainty_reason: A comparison of two analytic curves under one noise model, one study.
existing.reader_inference: The comparison uses ideal gates in the PCS analysis; the noisy-gate simulations in Figures 9 and 11 do not compare against BBPSSW.

existing.note: The abstract states it; Section II.A and the Introduction repeat it, citing earlier PCS work. The paper gives no resource count comparison beyond qubit counts in Section III.B.
existing.value: The authors state that PCS protects the targeted qubits and generally requires less resource overhead than standard quantum error correction and detection codes.
quotes: PCS provides protection on the targeted qubits and generally requires less resource overhead than standard quantum error correction and detection codes.
existing.certainty_reason: An author statement with citations to earlier work.

existing.note: Stated in the Introduction, Section III.B.4 and the Conclusions; the paper gives the code parameters and one generator but no full proof of the distance.
existing.value: The authors state that recursive PCS X&Z generates a family of distance 2 codes that are locally equivalent to CSS codes and have a maximum stabilizer generator weight of 4.
quotes: Recursive PCS X&Z generates a family of distance 2 codes that are locally equivalent to CSS codes and have a maximum stabilizer generator weight of 4.
existing.certainty_reason: Stated in the text without a written proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that Pauli check sandwiching uses symmetries of the payload unitary U to detect errors, and that the protocol is executed by measuring the ancilla in the Pauli Z basis and postselecting on the zero outcome.
quotes: In Pauli Check Sandwiching (PCS) we use symmetries of the payload unitary U to detect errors
The protocol is executed by measuring the ancilla in the Pauli Z basis and postselecting on the zero outcome.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of the scheme in Section II.A.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing earlier work, that in the theoretical limit of noiseless checks there exist checks, including non Pauli checks for general circuits, such that the postselected state is noiseless.
quotes: in the theoretical limit of noiseless checks, there exists checks (including non Pauli for general circuits) such that the postselected state is noiseless [11].
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to earlier work (its reference 11).

assertions.value: The authors state that the network PCS protocol has three steps: implement the left checks at the origin repeaters, send the flying qubits with their ancillas, and perform the right checks and postselect at the receiving repeater.
quotes: (1) implement the left checks at the origin repeaters on the qubits that will be sent, (2) send the flying qubits along with their ancillas, and (3) at the receiving repeater perform the right checks and postselect according to the standard PCS protocol.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of its distributed protocol in Section III.A.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the cases investigated PCS X&Z outperforms BBPSSW in fidelity for most of the domain while requiring fewer qubits, comparing against 2 rounds of BBPSSW with 8 qubits and 3 rounds with 16 qubits.
quotes: We compare PCS X&Z with 2 rounds of the BBPSSW protocol which uses 8 qubits and 3 rounds of BBPSSW which uses 16 qubits.
In the cases investigated, we outperform BBPSSW in terms of fidelity for most of the domain, while requiring less qubits.

assertions.value: The authors state that BBPSSW is not the best multi round protocol and that PCS X&Z, which uses 6 qubits, is not enough for the concatenated protocol that requires at least 8 qubits, so no comparison to that protocol is made.
quotes: Note that BBPSSW is not the best multi round protocol [21], since we can alternate between X and Z basis measurements for each round to achieve a higher fidelity.

assertions.value: The authors report that PCS X&Z and 3 round BBPSSW exhibit similar success probabilities, with PCS being slightly higher over most of the domain.

assertions.value: The authors state that the PCS equations cannot be applied recursively because the ancilla error rates are also determined by the input fidelity F, and that repeating the same checks on the same targets with a different ancilla should offer little benefit.

assertions.value: The authors state that in recursive PCS the recursion adds PCS X checks whose targets are the ancillas of the previous recursion, because Z errors on the ancillas are the errors that go undetected, and that each recursion level introduces two additional X checks.
quotes: we design a recursion scheme where the recursion is performed by adding more PCS checks, but the targets of the check gates are ancillas from the previous recursion.
Each recursion level introduces two additional X checks.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of the recursive scheme in Section III.B.3.

assertions.value: The authors state that the number of qubits and CNOT gates required for recursive PCS X&Z are only polynomial functions of the number of recursion levels, with the ancilla and CNOT cost for the right checks given by C(r) = 4(r + 1), where r is the recursion level.
quotes: The number of qubits and CNOT gates required for recursive PCS X&Z, are only polynomial functions of the number of recursion levels.
assertions.certainty_reason: A cost formula read from a circuit diagram; the text gives no derivation.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says the 4 appears because the circuit shows only one party; the plain count of 4 per level is the paper's own explanation.

assertions.value: The authors state that PCS X&Z can be considered a distance 1 code because it cannot detect an arbitrary single qubit error, but that it can detect arbitrary single qubit errors on the targeted qubits.
quotes: PCS X&Z can be considered a distance 1 code because it cannot detect an arbitrary single qubit error. However, PCS X&Z can detect arbitrary single qubit errors on the targeted qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement without a written proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that with 1 recursion the scheme forms a [[5, 1, 2]] code, with 2 recursions a [[7, 1, 2]] code, and in general a [[2(r - 1) + 5, 1, 2]] code for recursion r of at least 1.
quotes: With 1 recursion the scheme forms a [[5, 1, 2]] code. With 2 recursions the scheme forms a [[7, 1, 2]] code. Thus, this scheme generates a [[2(r − 1) + 5, 1, 2]] code for recursion r ≥ 1.
assertions.certainty_reason: The code parameters are stated without a written derivation.
assertions.reader_inference: The text writes the family as a [[2(r - 1) + 5, 1, 2]] code; with r = 1 this gives 5 and with r = 2 gives 7, matching its two named cases.
